name: Aaron Dessner
notes: Long Pond chamber-folk producer, and one of the fully documented entries in this section — studio, working method, harmonic philosophy, gear and specific production techniques are all sourced. The research names the backbeat class and says why it matters: "backbeat is half-time (on 3) or absent, which is the single biggest reason his records feel unlike the rest of this lane", so `halfTime` is true at `halftime_3` on the stated 68—90 core. Because the placement matches the parent, everything else carries the separation, and the entry supplies it: "drum machine, drum pads and subdued percussions and programmed drums rather than a kit; percussion is low in the mix and often enters only in the last third." That is a kick density of 1—2, the quietest velocity tier table in this whole section, `hihat.continuous` false at `fillDensity` 0.04 with the roll vocabulary off, a perc gain of —11 dB, and fills pushed to 16 bars. His harmonic philosophy is quoted directly and it is the rarest statement in the compendium: "I don't like major chords. I like the meditative patterns in certain prayers, and I like music that repeats itself." So every progression family is minor or modal, none is major, `susSubstitutionProb` is 0.52 and `ninth` is raised for the add9 voicings, `harmonicRhythm` is vamp-dominant with the longest chord windows here, and `melody.structure` is `riff_loop` because repetition is the stated structural principle. The bass is his documented device and it is not a groove: "multiple lushly harmonised basslines layered against a pulse — the bass is a harmonic voice, not a groove", which is `independent_riff` at `followRootsProb` 0.2 with the fullest passing-tone set on the producer side and chord-tone cells; there is no `bass808` block. "He initiates collaborations by sending an instrumental sketch first, so the harmony and arrangement predate the topline" is why the arrangement states the whole loop in an instrumental intro and has no big chorus — the peak is an orchestral swell, encoded as a long additive structure ending in a dissolving outro. The scale pool is the entry's "modal minor" and only that: `natural_minor` weighted over `dorian` and `phrygian`. `aeolian` is deliberately not listed as a fourth colour — engine/src/theory.rs resolves it to the same pitch collection as `natural_minor` (the test `aeolian_and_natural_minor_are_the_same_scale`), so listing both would advertise a mode this model does not have. ⚠ The INFERRED parameters are every drum probability, the velocity tiers, the humanize numbers, the `dorian`/`phrygian` split inside that "modal minor" and `bpm.mode` 79 (the midpoint of the stated 68—90 core). ⚠ **The countermelody reached 968/1000 distinct answers against a floor of 980 (2026-08-17, counter variety floor).** `melody.emptyBarBias` came down from 0.18 to 0.1. The counter's note count is `densityRatio` times the lead's own note count, so a bar the lead leaves empty is a bar the counter has nothing to answer — and one empty region is IDENTICAL to every other one, which is the single thing a seed cannot vary. Measured across this roster the models failing this gate average 0.150 here against 0.030 for the models that pass. ⚠ The value that moved here is INFERRED rather than a researched claim — the entry's Melody/chords line reads "sonorous piano, picked guitars (1965 Gibson Firebird, 1963 Fender Jazzmaster, 1972 Telecaster through vintage Fender/Ampeg amps), mandola, harmonium and string/horn orchestrations; loops are 4 or 8 bars. He initiates collaborations by sending an instrumental sketch first, so the harmony and arrangement predate the topline.", and every claim in it still holds after the change.
